blocks.t: Meaning and scope — POSDCORB vs subject-matter
blocks.x: The **managerial view** confines administration to common processes; the **subject-matter view** says each sector has its own substance.
blocks.th: **Gulick** (POSDCORB) against **Marshall Dimock**, who called POSDCORB 'a set of tools, not the substance'.
blocks.in: NITI's sectoral verticals against DoPT's common personnel rules.
blocks.gl: US OPM as process, sectoral departments as substance.
blocks.w: Both are partial: administration is **process plus purpose**, and the split explains the discipline's identity crisis.

blocks.x: They share techniques but differ in **ends, accountability and scale** — public administration acts under law, faces public scrutiny and pursues equity, not profit.
blocks.th: **Appleby** — 'government is different' because of its **political character, public accountability and breadth of scope**; **Sayre** — alike in all unimportant respects.
blocks.in: Air India before and after privatisation.
blocks.w: Difference is **constitutional, not technical**.

blocks.x: Administration is a **field of business** lying outside the proper sphere of politics; policy is decided politically and executed neutrally.
blocks.th: **Wilson (1887)**, sharpened by **Goodnow (1900)** — politics as the will of the state, administration as its execution.
blocks.in: The 'neutral versus committed bureaucracy' debate of the 1970s.
blocks.gl: US spoils system to merit under Pendleton, 1883.
blocks.w: Analytically useful, **empirically false** — administrators make policy daily.

blocks.x: Rejected value-neutrality and efficiency-worship; demanded that administration actively pursue **social equity**.
blocks.th: **Minnowbrook I (1968)** under **Waldo**; **Frederickson** made equity the **third pillar** beside efficiency and economy.
blocks.in: Reservation in services, Aspirational Districts, targeted subsidy.
blocks.w: Its four anchors — **relevance, values, social equity, change** — are the standard critique of a purely managerial state.

blocks.x: Treats the citizen as customer and imports market discipline: contracting out, performance measurement, agencification.
blocks.th: **Hood (1991)**, seven doctrines; **Osborne and Gaebler** — 'steering rather than rowing'.
blocks.in: Smart Cities SPVs, outcome budgeting, PPP in highways.
blocks.gl: UK Next Steps agencies, New Zealand's reforms.
blocks.w: Delivers speed, but **hollows out accountability** — the Smart Cities SPV bypassed the elected council.

blocks.x: The corrective to NPM: **serve citizens, not customers; seek the public interest; value citizenship over entrepreneurship**.
blocks.th: **Denhardt and Denhardt (2000)**, seven principles.
blocks.in: Social audit under MGNREGA, Gram Sabha planning, Sevottam.
blocks.w: The citizen is a **bearer of rights, not a consumer of services** — the sentence that closes any NPM answer.

blocks.x: Governance is the exercise of authority; **good** governance adds participation, transparency, accountability, rule of law, responsiveness and equity.
blocks.th: **World Bank (1992)**; UNESCAP's **eight characteristics**.
blocks.in: RTI, Citizens' Charters, DARPG's Good Governance Index; the 'minimum government, maximum governance' formulation.
blocks.w: It shifts the test from **inputs to outcomes and process legitimacy**.

blocks.x: The state steers **self-organising inter-organisational networks** rather than commanding hierarchies; resources are interdependent.
blocks.th: **Rhodes** — 'governing without government'; **Osborne's New Public Governance** completes PA → NPM → NPG.
blocks.in: NHM's convergence of state, NGO and private providers; PPP.
blocks.w: Networks buy capacity and **cost accountability** — the classic 'many hands' problem.

blocks.x: Bureaucrats maximise **budget, staff and discretion**, not the public interest, so competition and exit rights must discipline them.
blocks.th: **Niskanen** (budget-maximising bureau), **Buchanan and Tullock**; **Vincent Ostrom's** polycentricity.
blocks.in: Disinvestment policy, school vouchers debate, DBT replacing in-kind delivery.
blocks.w: Intellectual parent of NPM; criticised for assuming **self-interest is the only motive**.

blocks.x: Administration is shaped by its environment — no system can be transplanted intact.
blocks.th: **Riggs**; **John Gaus's** seven factors — people, place, physical technology, social technology, wishes and ideas, catastrophe, personality.
blocks.in: Why the Collector's colonial design persists in a democratic republic.
blocks.gl: Failed transplants of Westminster models in post-colonial Africa.
blocks.w: Any reform proposal must state **what in the Indian context will carry it**.

blocks.t: Administration as a discipline — the paradigms
blocks.x: Five stages: dichotomy (1900-26), principles (1927-37), political science (1950-70), management science (1956-70), and **public administration as itself** from 1970.
blocks.th: **Nicholas Henry**.
blocks.in: IIPA (1954) and the growth of PA as a university subject.
blocks.w: The discipline's history is a search for **identity between politics and management**.

blocks.x: Legitimacy now rests on **responsiveness and participation**, not only legality.
blocks.th: **Frederickson's** equity; **Arnstein's ladder of participation** — from manipulation to citizen control.
blocks.in: Gram Sabha, ward committees, social audit, MyGov consultation.
blocks.w: Ask **where on Arnstein's ladder** a scheme actually sits — most Indian 'participation' stops at consultation.

blocks.x: Development needs all three; the debate is over the **boundary**, not the existence, of each.
blocks.th: **Evans's 'embedded autonomy'**; the strong state versus market debate.
blocks.in: Liberalisation of 1991, the regulatory state, SHGs and NGOs in delivery.
blocks.w: India moved from **producer state to regulatory state** without building regulatory capacity first.

blocks.x: A colonial steel frame carrying a welfare and developmental mandate it was never designed for.
blocks.th: **Waldo's administrative state**; **Riggs's prismatic society**.
blocks.in: Collector as revenue officer, magistrate, development coordinator and DDMA chair at once.
blocks.w: The tension between **regulatory inheritance and developmental mandate** is Paper II's central theme.

blocks.x: One best way, discovered by **time and motion study**; scientific selection, training, functional foremanship and differential piece-rate.
blocks.th: **F.W. Taylor (1911)**, seeking a **'mental revolution'** between labour and management.
blocks.in: Work-study cells, O&M divisions, e-Office time norms.
blocks.w: Raised productivity but treated the worker as an **economic animal** and ignored the informal group.

blocks.x: Management seen from the top: **POCCC** and fourteen principles including unity of command, scalar chain with the **gangplank**, and esprit de corps.
blocks.th: **Henri Fayol (1916)**.
blocks.in: Secretariat hierarchy and the file's scalar journey; the gangplank is what the desk officer system tries to institutionalise.
blocks.w: Complements Taylor: **shop floor upward versus office downward**.

blocks.x: Hierarchy, division of labour, written rules, impersonality, technical qualification, career service, office separated from person — resting on **legal-rational authority**.
blocks.th: **Max Weber**; 'technically superior to any other form', yet an **iron cage** of rationality.
blocks.in: The steel frame; Article 311 protection; seniority-bound careers.
blocks.w: An **ideal type**, not a description — its value is as a yardstick, not a portrait.

blocks.x: Rules meant to secure reliability produce rigidity and displaced goals.
blocks.th: **Merton** — trained incapacity, goal displacement, ritualism; **Selznick** — sub-unit goals and co-optation (TVA); **Gouldner** — mock, representative and punishment-centred bureaucracy; **Crozier** — the vicious circle; **Michels** — iron law of oligarchy.
blocks.in: File-as-objective; committees multiplying after every scandal.
blocks.w: Name the **specific pathology**, not 'red tape'.

blocks.x: The bridge to human relations: **'power with' not 'power over'**, the **law of the situation**, and **integration** as the best conflict resolution.
blocks.th: **Follett**; four principles of coordination — direct contact, early stage, reciprocal relationship, continuous process.
blocks.in: Inter-departmental coordination committees; the DM's conflict role.
blocks.w: Obey **the situation, not the person** — authority follows knowledge.

blocks.x: Output depends on **social norms and the informal group**, not physical conditions alone; being observed itself changes behaviour.
blocks.th: **Mayo**, Hawthorne experiments (1924-32) — illumination, relay assembly, interviewing, bank wiring room.
blocks.in: Informal networks and unions in field offices; morale in police lines.
blocks.w: Criticised as **'cow sociology'** — managerial bias, conflict ignored.

blocks.x: Administration is **decision-making**; the 'principles' are mere **proverbs**, each with an equally plausible opposite.
blocks.th: **Simon (1947)** — bounded rationality, **satisficing**, fact-value dichotomy, decision premises, zone of acceptance; Nobel 1978.
blocks.in: A Collector choosing under incomplete data and conflicting statutes.
blocks.w: Improve the **premises of decision**, since full rationality is unattainable.

blocks.x: Organisation as a **cooperative system**; authority rests on the subordinate's acceptance within a **zone of indifference**.
blocks.th: **Barnard (1938)** — the executive maintains communication, secures essential services, formulates purpose; effectiveness (goal) versus efficiency (individual satisfaction).
blocks.in: Why an unpopular transfer order still moves; why some orders quietly die.
blocks.w: **Authority flows upward** from acceptance, not downward from rank.

blocks.x: **Theory X** assumes dislike of work needing coercion; **Theory Y** assumes self-direction toward committed objectives.
blocks.th: **McGregor (1960)** — managerial assumption as a self-fulfilling prophecy.
blocks.in: Attendance-biometrics culture versus outcome-based appraisal.
blocks.w: The style you choose **manufactures the behaviour** you then cite to justify it.

blocks.x: Maslow ranks needs from physiological to self-actualisation; Herzberg splits **hygiene factors** (pay, policy, supervision) from **motivators** (achievement, recognition, the work itself).
blocks.th: **Maslow (1943)**, **Herzberg**.
blocks.in: Pay commissions address hygiene; Mission Karmayogi's role-based work addresses motivators.
blocks.w: In a fixed-pay service, only **motivators** are available — hence job enrichment, not enlargement.

blocks.x: Argyris: formal hierarchy keeps adults **dependent and passive**, clashing with mature personality. Likert: four systems, culminating in **participative group (System 4)** with the **linking pin**.
blocks.th: **Chris Argyris**, **Rensis Likert**.
blocks.in: Cutting the levels a file crosses; team-based district task forces.
blocks.w: Structure itself can **infantilise** competent officers.

blocks.x: Policy proceeds by **successive limited comparisons** from the status quo, because comprehensive rationality is impossible.
blocks.th: **Lindblom (1959)** — 'the science of muddling through'; partisan mutual adjustment; later disjointed incrementalism.
blocks.in: Annual budget increments; slow amendment of the Police Act, 1861.
blocks.w: Realistic but **conservative** — it cannot deliver a break with the past.

blocks.x: Scan broadly for **fundamental** decisions and in detail for **incremental** ones — the doctor's approach, not the mechanic's.
blocks.th: **Etzioni (1967)**; also his compliance typology — coercive, remunerative, normative power matched to alienative, calculative, moral involvement.
blocks.in: A Five Year Plan's broad scan against annual allocations.
blocks.w: The **synthesis** between Simon's rationality and Lindblom's incrementalism.

blocks.x: Transitional societies are **prismatic** — heterogeneous, formalistic, with overlapping modern and traditional structures; the **sala** is its office.
blocks.th: **Fred Riggs**; also the bazaar-canteen economy and poly-communalism.
blocks.in: Charters without remedies; rules notified but unenforced; caste and kinship inside a legal-rational office.
blocks.w: **Formalism** — the gap between the prescribed and the practised — is the concept to name.

blocks.x: The **saptanga** seven limbs of the state; the ruler's dharma is **yogakshema**, pursued through proportionate **danda**.
blocks.th: **Arthashastra** — 'in the happiness of his subjects lies the king's happiness'; and the honey-on-the-tongue warning on official corruption.
blocks.in: Cited as India's indigenous administrative theory against a Western-only canon.
blocks.w: India had a **theory of administration** two millennia before Wilson.

blocks.x: Four models in ascending realism: **rational-comprehensive, incremental, mixed scanning, garbage can**.
blocks.th: **Simon, Lindblom, Etzioni, Cohen-March-Olsen**.
blocks.in: GST design (rational), annual budget (incremental), Five Year Plans (mixed), a scheme repurposed mid-course (garbage can).
blocks.w: Name all four, then justify **which one the case actually fits**.

blocks.x: In **organised anarchies**, problems, solutions, participants and choice opportunities are dumped together and coupled almost randomly — **solutions chase problems**.
blocks.th: **Cohen, March and Olsen (1972)**.
blocks.in: A scheme designed for one purpose deployed for another; committees formed to absorb a crisis.
blocks.w: Explains the **irrationality** that incrementalism still assumes away.

blocks.x: Content theories say **what** motivates (Maslow, Herzberg, McClelland); process theories say **how** (Vroom, Adams).
blocks.th: **Vroom** — motivation = expectancy × instrumentality × valence; **Adams** — equity as a ratio against a referent.
blocks.in: Appraisal with no consequence breaks instrumentality; pay-parity grievances are equity theory.
blocks.gl: Performance-related pay in the UK civil service.
blocks.w: In public service, **valence must come from purpose**, since reward is fixed.

blocks.x: Achievement, affiliation and power — and **institutionalised power** is the motive that predicts effective managers.
blocks.th: **David McClelland**.
blocks.in: Officers who build institutions versus those who build personal followings.
blocks.w: The distinction between **personalised and socialised power** is the one to write.

blocks.x: Trait → behavioural (**Blake and Mouton's grid**, 9,9 team management) → situational (**Hersey-Blanchard**, matched to follower maturity) → **transformational**.
blocks.th: **Burns and Bass** — idealised influence, inspirational motivation, intellectual stimulation, individualised consideration.
blocks.in: E. Sreedharan and Verghese Kurien as transformational; routine transfers as transactional.
blocks.w: There is **no one best style** — the situation selects it.

blocks.x: Formal versus the **grapevine**; downward, upward, horizontal and diagonal flows; barriers semantic, psychological, organisational and status-related.
blocks.th: **Barnard** — maintaining communication is the executive's first function.
blocks.in: e-Office and file noting as the formal channel; the informal 'note on file' culture.
blocks.w: Upward communication fails first, because it carries **bad news**.

blocks.x: **Motivation** is individual drive; **morale** is the group's collective attitude — high motivation can coexist with low morale and vice versa.
blocks.th: Human relations school.
blocks.in: Police lines and paramilitary postings; CAPF suicide and attrition data.
blocks.w: Treat morale as **an institutional variable**, not the sum of individual moods.

blocks.x: A cohesive group suppresses dissent to preserve consensus, producing illusions of invulnerability and unanimity, and self-appointed **mindguards**.
blocks.th: **Irving Janis**.
blocks.in: Committee decisions where no member records a dissent; intelligence failures.
blocks.w: Remedies: a **devil's advocate**, independent evaluation, anonymous objection channel.

blocks.x: Conflict is **inevitable and not always dysfunctional**; the question is the mode of handling it.
blocks.th: **Follett** — domination, compromise, **integration**; **Thomas-Kilmann** — competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating.
blocks.in: Centre-state disputes, inter-departmental turf, line-staff friction.
blocks.w: **Integration** finds the interest behind the position; compromise merely splits it.

blocks.x: The bureaucratic personality is **made, not born** — structure shapes conduct.
blocks.th: **Merton** on trained incapacity; **Argyris** on the immaturity forced by hierarchy; **Zimbardo** on situational roles.
blocks.in: The same officer who is rigid at a counter is inventive in a disaster — the role, not the person, changed.
blocks.w: Reform the **situation** before judging the personality.

blocks.x: Self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skill — the competencies that decide whether authority is used well.
blocks.th: **Goleman**.
blocks.in: Mission Karmayogi's behavioural competencies; crowd handling by a magistrate.
blocks.gl: Leadership development in the OECD services.
blocks.w: Empathy makes **grievance redress real** rather than procedural.

blocks.x: **Classical** (structure, Fayol-Gulick), **neo-classical** (informal group, Mayo), **modern** — systems, contingency and post-modern.
blocks.th: **Katz and Kahn** — organisation as an **open system** with inputs, throughput, outputs, feedback and **equifinality**.
blocks.in: A district administration as an open system absorbing political, social and climatic inputs.
blocks.w: Classical assumed a **closed system**; that assumption is its fatal flaw.

blocks.x: **No one best way** — structure must fit environment, technology and task.
blocks.th: **Burns and Stalker** (mechanistic for stable, organic for turbulent); **Lawrence and Lorsch** (differentiation and integration); **Woodward** (technology).
blocks.in: A regulatory office can be mechanistic; a disaster response cell must be organic.
blocks.w: The theoretical answer to Simon's demolition of universal principles.

blocks.x: **Line** performs the primary purpose; **staff** advises without command; **auxiliary** supplies common services.
blocks.th: Classical organisation theory.
blocks.in: Line — district administration; staff — Cabinet Secretariat, planning cells; auxiliary — GeM, CPWD, printing.
blocks.gl: US Executive Office of the President as staff.
blocks.w: Line-staff conflict arises from **staff assuming implied authority** — the remedy is a written charter.

blocks.x: **Political versus permanent, single versus plural, real versus nominal**.
blocks.th: Comparative organisation theory.
blocks.in: President and Governor are nominal; the Council of Ministers is real (*Shamsher Singh*, 1974). ECI is plural, CAG single.
blocks.gl: US President single, Swiss Federal Council plural.
blocks.w: Plural heads secure **deliberation**; single heads secure **speed and accountability**.

blocks.x: **Departmental undertaking** — full control, least autonomy; **public corporation** — by statute, autonomy with accountability; **government company** — under the Companies Act, most flexible.
blocks.th: Public enterprise theory.
blocks.in: Railways (department), FCI and LIC (corporation), most PSUs (company under Section 2(45)).
blocks.w: Autonomy rises and **direct legislative control falls** across the three.

blocks.x: Used where **impartiality, expertise or continuity** outweigh the need for single-point speed.
blocks.th: Organisation theory on plural bodies.
blocks.in: UPSC, ECI, Finance Commission, regulatory commissions.
blocks.w: They **trade speed for insulation** — that trade is their justification.

blocks.x: Field agencies know the terrain, headquarters knows the policy; friction is structural, not personal.
blocks.th: **Deconcentration** distinguished from **decentralisation**.
blocks.in: Ministry versus attached and subordinate offices; the **tenure system** that rotates officers between the two.
blocks.w: The tenure system exists to keep the secretariat **in touch with field reality**.

blocks.x: **Delegation** transfers specified powers while responsibility is retained; **deconcentration** disperses offices; **decentralisation** shifts authority downward; **devolution** transfers functions, funds and functionaries to an autonomous elected body.
blocks.th: Public administration theory; **subsidiarity** as the underlying principle.
blocks.in: The 73rd and 74th Amendments are devolution in form, delegation in practice.
blocks.w: Precision here **is** the answer — most scripts blur the four.

blocks.x: The number of subordinates one superior can effectively supervise; relationships multiply geometrically as it grows.
blocks.th: **Graicunas's** formula; **Urwick** suggested five or six at the top.
blocks.in: Flattening the levels a file crosses from seven to four under e-Office.
blocks.w: Technology has made the classical narrow span **obsolete**.

blocks.x: **Formal** authority flows from position, **acceptance** from the subordinate, **competence** from knowledge.
blocks.th: **Weber/Fayol**, **Barnard**, **Follett**; **French and Raven's** five bases — legitimate, reward, coercive, expert, referent.
blocks.in: Public service relies on legitimate and expert power, having little reward power.
blocks.w: Scarcity of reward power is exactly why **motivation theory** matters in government.

blocks.x: The designed structure of roles, and the network of personal relationships that actually carries information.
blocks.th: **Barnard** — informal organisation is **necessary to the operation of the formal**; Mayo's bank wiring room.
blocks.in: Batch and cadre loyalties; the grapevine in a secretariat.
blocks.w: Suppressing the informal does not remove it — it **drives it underground**.

blocks.x: Three levels — visible artefacts, espoused values, and **basic assumptions** that are taken for granted.
blocks.th: **Edgar Schein**; **Lewin's** unfreeze-change-refreeze.
blocks.in: Mission Karmayogi's attempt to shift from rule-based to role-based behaviour.
blocks.w: Reform fails at the level of **basic assumptions**, not of artefacts.

blocks.x: **Displacement** (means become ends), **succession** (a new goal after the original is met), **multiplication** (goals added).
blocks.th: **Merton**, **Michels**; the March of Dimes as the classic succession case.
blocks.in: A scheme continuing after its purpose is served; targets replacing outcomes.
blocks.w: Each names a **different institutional drift** — pick the right one.

blocks.x: A permanent, expert, hierarchical body inside a system founded on periodic popular consent — the standing tension of the discipline.
blocks.th: **Weber** on the politician-official relation; **Finer versus Friedrich** on external control against inner professional responsibility.
blocks.in: Neutral versus committed bureaucracy; ministerial responsibility in practice.
blocks.w: **Finer** wants control; **Friedrich** trusts professionalism — India needs both.

blocks.x: **Responsibility** is the obligation to perform; **accountability** the obligation to answer to someone who can sanction; **answerability** without sanction is only reporting.
blocks.th: Administrative theory; **Finer** on external accountability.
blocks.in: NHRC recommendations and CAG findings carry no enforcement — reporting, not accountability.
blocks.w: Reporting is not accountability **unless someone must answer and can be sanctioned**.

blocks.x: **Vertical** (elections, citizen action), **horizontal** (CAG, CVC, judiciary, legislature), **social** (social audit, RTI, report cards), **diagonal** (citizens inside horizontal bodies).
blocks.th: Governance theory.
blocks.in: Social audit under MGNREGA; Meghalaya's 2017 Act; CPGRAMS feedback.
blocks.gl: Citizen report cards, Bangalore and beyond.
blocks.w: Name the **type** before prescribing the remedy.

blocks.x: Through questions, motions, debates, and above all **committees** — PAC, Estimates, COPU and the department-related standing committees.
blocks.th: Parliamentary control theory.
blocks.in: PAC examines the CAG's report; Estimates looks forward at economy; the **guillotine** passes most demands without discussion.
blocks.w: Control is **post-facto and selective** — the guillotine is the honest limit to state.

blocks.x: Hierarchy, inspection, budgetary and personnel control, vigilance, and performance appraisal.
blocks.th: Classical control theory.
blocks.in: Annual inspections, ACR to PAR, CVO network, transfers as the informal control.
blocks.w: Transfer used as **punishment** converts control into political interference.

blocks.x: Through **writs, judicial review of administrative action, and the principles of natural justice**.
blocks.th: **A.K. Kraipak (1969)** applied natural justice to administrative action; **Maneka (1978)** made procedure just, fair and reasonable.
blocks.in: *L. Chandra Kumar* preserving High Court review over tribunals.
blocks.w: Judicial control is **remedial and episodic** — it cannot substitute for internal control.

blocks.x: A published statement of service standards with the six principles — quality, choice, standards, value, accountability, transparency.
blocks.th: UK, 1991; India from 1997; **Sevottam** as the Indian delivery model.
blocks.in: Second ARC found charters drafted without consulting citizens or staff and carrying no remedy.
blocks.gl: UK Citizen's Charter and its successor programmes.
blocks.w: A charter binds only when default carries a **personal financial consequence** — hence the Public Service Guarantee Acts.

blocks.x: Converts secrecy-by-default into disclosure-by-default; **Section 4 proactive disclosure** is its ethical heart.
blocks.th: MKSS's jan sunwai movement; the Act of 2005.
blocks.in: 45-60 lakh applications a year; vacancies in Information Commissions blunt it; the 2019 amendment took tenure and salary powers to the Centre; DPDP narrowed 8(1)(j).
blocks.gl: FOIA in the US and Sweden's 1766 principle.
blocks.w: Transparency was **won from below**, and is being narrowed from above.

blocks.x: The community verifies expenditure against work done, in public.
blocks.th: Participatory accountability theory.
blocks.in: MGNREGA Section 17; **SSAAT Andhra Pradesh** with independent village auditors; **Meghalaya Act, 2017** made it statutory across departments.
blocks.w: It works only when the auditor is **independent of the implementing agency**.

blocks.x: Disclosure of wrongdoing by an insider, needing protection from retaliation.
blocks.th: Ethics of disclosure — gravity, evidence, exhaustion of internal channels, proportionality.
blocks.in: **Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 never brought into force**; Satyendra Dubey and Manjunath as the cost of that gap.
blocks.gl: US False Claims Act with qui tam rewards.
blocks.w: A law that exists **on paper only** is the sharpest example of formalism.

blocks.x: An independent anti-corruption ombudsman with inquiry, prosecution and attachment powers.
blocks.th: Origin in the **First ARC (1966)**; Swedish ombudsman as the model.
blocks.in: Act of 2013; first Lokpal only in **2019**; jurisdiction over the PM with exclusions; states required to create Lokayuktas within a year.
blocks.w: Institutional design was achieved; **outcomes were not** — the gap is the answer.

blocks.x: CVC supervises vigilance; the CBI investigates, resting only on the **DSPE Act, 1946**, not its own statute.
blocks.th: **Santhanam Committee (1964)** created the CVC; **Vineet Narain (1997)** insulated the CBI.
blocks.in: Two-year minimum tenure for the Director; **states withdrawing general consent** under Section 6.
blocks.w: The CBI's fragility is **statutory**, not managerial.

blocks.x: **Corruption = Monopoly + Discretion − Accountability**.
blocks.th: **Klitgaard's** equation; Second ARC — corruption is 'a low-risk, high-reward activity'.
blocks.in: e-procurement, GeM, faceless assessment and DBT all attack monopoly and discretion.
blocks.w: Write the equation, then show **which term the reform attacks**.

blocks.x: Fixing the system that allowed the wrong, rather than only punishing the person who exploited it.
blocks.th: CVC's own emphasis; systems view of integrity.
blocks.in: Transparency of rates, rotation of sensitive posts, technology-mediated transactions, Vigilance Awareness Week.
blocks.gl: Integrity Pact in defence procurement (Transparency International).
blocks.w: Preventive vigilance earns more marks than punitive — it addresses **cause, not symptom**.

blocks.t: Media, interest groups and civil society
blocks.x: External, non-state instruments of accountability that work through exposure rather than sanction.
blocks.th: Pressure group typology — institutional, associational, anomic, non-associational; the **iron triangle**.
blocks.in: RTI activists, ADR's affidavits analysis, PIL, investigative journalism; FCRA restrictions as the counter-pressure.
blocks.gl: Investigative press and NGOs in OECD states.
blocks.w: Their power is **agenda-setting**; enforcement still needs the state.

blocks.x: The law governing the **powers, procedures and control** of administrative authorities — it grows wherever the state acts on the citizen.
blocks.th: **Dicey** initially denied its existence in England; **droit administratif** in France showed otherwise.
blocks.in: Expansion of the welfare and regulatory state made it unavoidable.
blocks.gl: French Conseil d'État as a separate administrative jurisdiction.
blocks.w: Administrative law is the price of the **administrative state**.

blocks.x: **Supremacy of law, equality before law, and rights derived from ordinary law** — Dicey's three meanings.
blocks.th: **A.V. Dicey**; criticised for ignoring necessary discretion and for misreading droit administratif.
blocks.in: Article 14; judicial review as basic structure; *Kesavananda*'s rule-of-law element.
blocks.w: Modern rule of law accommodates **discretion bounded by criteria and reasons**.

blocks.x: Rule-making by the executive under a parent Act — necessary in a technical state, dangerous without limits.
blocks.th: **Delhi Laws Act (1951)** — **essential legislative functions cannot be delegated**; the legislature must lay down policy and standard.
blocks.in: Volume of rules far exceeds primary legislation; the **Committee on Subordinate Legislation** scrutinises a fraction.
blocks.gl: Henry VIII clauses in the UK.
blocks.w: The gap is not delegation but **scrutiny capacity**.

blocks.x: Unavoidable because rules cannot foresee every case; dangerous because it is where arbitrariness enters.
blocks.th: **Wade**; Indian control through Article 14's **non-arbitrariness** (*E.P. Royappa*).
blocks.in: Licensing, transfers, sanction of prosecution, discretionary quotas.
blocks.w: The remedy is not abolition but **criteria stated in advance, reasons recorded, and review**.

blocks.x: **Nemo judex in causa sua** and **audi alteram partem**, with the modern addition of a **reasoned order**.
blocks.th: **A.K. Kraipak (1969)** blurred the quasi-judicial/administrative line; **Maneka (1978)** made audi alteram partem implicit in Article 21.
blocks.in: Departmental inquiries under Article 311; show-cause notices; blacklisting.
blocks.w: Natural justice now attaches to **administrative action affecting rights**, not just quasi-judicial acts.

blocks.x: Tribunals decide disputes with speed, expertise and low cost, at the price of uniform procedure and independence.
blocks.th: **Articles 323A and 323B** (42nd Amendment); *L. Chandra Kumar* (1997) preserved High Court review as basic structure.
blocks.in: CAT, NCLT, NGT, TDSAT; *Rojer Mathew* struck down executive control over appointments and tenure; **National Tribunals Commission** repeatedly directed and never created.
blocks.gl: UK tribunals service after the Leggatt review.

blocks.w: Use Riggs as a **diagnostic vocabulary**, not as a prophecy.

blocks.w: India inherited a **prefectoral field system inside a parliamentary shell**.

blocks.in: Strong permanent executive alongside weak local political capacity.
blocks.w: Where politics is weak, **administration fills the vacuum** — and that is a democratic problem.

blocks.x: Administration **for** planned socio-economic change — change-oriented, goal-oriented, innovative, client-oriented, time-bound.

blocks.x: Weberian bureaucracy secures predictability but can be too rigid for developmental improvisation.

blocks.in: 1991 liberalisation; PLI as industrial policy returning; the shift from producer to regulatory state.

blocks.th: Regulatory state theory; **regulatory capture**.
blocks.in: SEBI, TRAI, CERC, CCI, RERA; disinvestment; PPP.
blocks.w: India **created regulators faster than it built regulatory capacity**.

blocks.x: From welfare → equity → anti-poverty → efficiency → empowerment; and from **WID to GAD** — treating gender relations, not women, as the unit.

blocks.in: Kudumbashree, SHG-bank linkage, Lakhpati Didi, one-third and now half reservation in panchayats.
blocks.w: Ask whether a scheme meets **practical needs or strategic interests** — the distinction is the mark.

blocks.x: Participation ranges from token consultation to genuine citizen control.

blocks.in: Gram Sabha, PESA consent, JFM committees, pani panchayats, ward committees.
blocks.w: Most Indian participation stops at **consultation** — say where on the ladder it sits.

blocks.t: Role of NGOs and civil society

blocks.x: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
blocks.th: **Brundtland (1987)**; SDGs 2030 with 17 goals.

blocks.gl: UN 2030 Agenda; only ~17% of targets on track.
blocks.w: Administration's task is **integrating three ledgers** — economic, social, ecological.

blocks.x: People, not structures, deliver — so recruitment, training, motivation and career design are the real levers.

blocks.in: Mission Karmayogi's shift from **rule-based to role-based** competence via the FRAC model.
blocks.w: Capacity spent at the **cutting edge** returns more than capacity spent at the top.

blocks.x: **Position** classification grades the job and recruits to it; **career/rank** classification recruits to a service and moves the person through posts.
blocks.th: Comparative personnel administration.
blocks.in: India follows the career model — mobility and continuity, but weak specialisation.
blocks.w: Career systems produce **generalists by design**, which is why domain reform keeps returning.

blocks.x: Whether policy posts need domain expertise or coordinating skill.
blocks.th: **Fulton Committee (1968)** attacked the 'cult of the amateur'; Second ARC recommended domain assignment.
blocks.in: Hota (2004), Baswan (2016), lateral entry from 2018, Mission Karmayogi.
blocks.gl: UK Civil Service College and unified grading.
blocks.w: The real question is **at what level and for what decision** — not who is superior.

blocks.x: Open competitive examination as the guarantee of merit and insulation from patronage.
blocks.th: **Northcote-Trevelyan (1854)**; **Pendleton Act (1883)** ended the spoils system.
blocks.in: UPSC under Articles 315-323; Kothari (1976) designed the present three-stage scheme; Alagh (2001) led to CSAT.
blocks.w: Merit recruitment is the **foundation of neutrality**, not merely of quality.

blocks.x: Induction, mid-career and specialised — building competence and a shared institutional ethic.
blocks.th: National Training Policy 1996 and 2012; **FRAC** competency framework.
blocks.in: LBSNAA, SVPNPA, IGNFA, ISTM, NIFM; **Aarambh** common foundation course; iGOT with 1 crore+ users.
blocks.w: Training changes behaviour only when **posting and appraisal reward it**.

blocks.x: From the confidential ACR to the disclosed, numerically graded **PAR**, with 360-degree input for empanelment.
blocks.th: **Surinder Nath Committee (2003)**.
blocks.in: Rating inflation means almost everyone is 'outstanding', so promotion reverts to seniority.
blocks.gl: Performance management in the UK and Australia.
blocks.w: An appraisal with **no consequence** produces no motivation — Vroom's instrumentality fails.

blocks.x: Seniority secures predictability and morale; merit secures capability — India blends them with benchmarks.
blocks.th: Personnel theory; **MACP** for assured career progression.
blocks.in: Empanelment at Joint Secretary and above through 360-degree feedback; two intensive reviews recommended at 14 and 20 years by the Second ARC.
blocks.gl: Senior Executive Service selection in the US.
blocks.w: Seniority is fair; **merit is developmental** — the balance is the policy question.

blocks.x: Pay must be adequate, equitable and comparable; it is a hygiene factor whose absence demotivates.
blocks.th: **Herzberg**; **Adams's equity theory**.
blocks.in: **7th CPC** pay matrix replacing bands and grade pay; 8th CPC announced; **Unified Pension Scheme (2025)** giving an assured 50% after 25 years.
blocks.w: Pension design is simultaneously a **motivation instrument and a fiscal liability**.

blocks.t: Discipline and the doctrine of pleasure
blocks.x: Article 310 holds servants at pleasure; **Article 311** limits it with inquiry and reasonable opportunity, subject to three exceptions.

blocks.in: AIS (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1969; departmental inquiries.
blocks.gl: UK dismissal at pleasure without equivalent protection.
blocks.w: India's pleasure doctrine is **far more constrained** than the English rule.

blocks.x: Public servants have association rights but **no right to strike**.
blocks.th: **T.K. Rangarajan (2003)** — no fundamental, statutory or moral right to strike.
blocks.in: **Joint Consultative Machinery and Compulsory Arbitration (1966)** as the constructive channel; service associations.
blocks.gl: Collective bargaining rights in Scandinavian public services.
blocks.w: Denial of strike must be matched by a **functioning negotiation machinery**.

blocks.x: The Westminster trio — serve any government faithfully, advise in private, take no public credit or blame.
blocks.th: **Sardar Patel** on independence of expression and fearlessness; the 1970s 'committed bureaucracy' debate.
blocks.in: Conduct Rules bar public criticism of policy; officers writing op-eds and joining politics test anonymity.
blocks.w: Commitment is owed to the **Constitution**, not to a party programme.

blocks.x: Integrity is sustained by systems, not exhortation.
blocks.th: **Nolan's seven principles**; Second ARC's 'Ethics in Governance'.
blocks.in: Conduct Rules (AIS 1968, CCS 1964), asset disclosure, Integrity Pact, preventive vigilance.
blocks.gl: UK Committee on Standards in Public Life.
blocks.w: India is **conduct-rule heavy and ethics-code light** — the Second ARC's core criticism.

blocks.x: Fixed tenure, transparent transfers and written orders as the structural protection of honest officers.
blocks.th: **T.S.R. Subramanian (2013)** — Civil Services Board, minimum tenure, **oral instructions to be recorded in writing**.
blocks.in: Partial compliance by states; Khemka's 50+ transfers as the cost of non-compliance.
blocks.gl: Merit protection boards in the US.
blocks.w: Written orders convert **pressure into evidence** — the most practical safeguard there is.

blocks.x: A service mirroring society's composition is more responsive and more legitimate.
blocks.th: **Kingsley**, **Krislov**; **passive** representation (composition) versus **active** (advocacy).
blocks.in: Reservation in services — the world's largest such experiment; women ~12% of the police against a declared 33%.
blocks.gl: US affirmative action in federal employment.
blocks.w: Passive representation matters because it changes **what the institution notices**.

blocks.x: **Rational, incremental, mixed scanning, garbage can**, plus **elite, group, institutional and systems** models.
blocks.th: Simon, Lindblom, Etzioni, Cohen-March-Olsen; **Easton's** input-output system with feedback.
blocks.in: GST as near-rational; police reform as blocked incrementalism.
blocks.w: State the model, then show **why this case fits it** — that is the whole answer.

blocks.x: A discipline that is **problem-oriented, contextual and multi-disciplinary**, with seven decision stages.
blocks.th: **Harold Lasswell**; politics as 'who gets what, when and how'.
blocks.in: NITI's evidence-based policy push; DMEO evaluations.
blocks.w: Policy science was founded to be **useful**, not merely descriptive.

blocks.x: **Distributive** (low conflict), **redistributive** (high conflict), **regulatory**, **constituent** — and **policy determines politics**.
blocks.th: **Theodore Lowi**.
blocks.in: Subsidies distributive; reservation and progressive tax redistributive; environmental standards regulatory; creating a commission constituent.
blocks.w: Predict the **conflict level** from the policy type before predicting implementation.

blocks.t: Agenda setting and the policy window
blocks.x: Problems, policies and politics flow separately; change comes when an entrepreneur **couples** them at an open window.
blocks.th: **Kingdon's multiple streams**.
blocks.in: GST, IBC and Aadhaar each waited years for the window; COVID opened windows for telemedicine and DPI.
blocks.w: The best frame for **'why did this reform happen now'**.

blocks.x: Policy change follows shifts in coalitions bound by **shared belief systems**, over a decade or more.
blocks.th: **Sabatier**.
blocks.in: The coalition around RTI; the shifting coalition on nuclear liability.
blocks.w: Explains change that is **too slow for Kingdon and too big for incrementalism**.

blocks.x: Success needs clear objectives, sound causal theory, few clearance points, committed implementers and a stable context.
blocks.th: **Pressman and Wildavsky (1973)** — the multiplication of probabilities across clearance points; **Sabatier-Mazmanian's** conditions.
blocks.in: A CSS passing through ministry, state, district, block and panchayat — each a clearance point.
blocks.w: Convergence models succeed by **collapsing clearance points**, not by adding committees.

blocks.x: Policy is actually made by frontline discretion under resource pressure.
blocks.th: **Lipsky's street-level bureaucracy**; Hjern; Elmore's **backward mapping**.
blocks.in: Patwari, ASHA, constable, anganwadi worker and panchayat secretary — widest discretion, least training.
blocks.w: Coping mechanisms are **rational responses to scarcity**, not attitude problems.

blocks.x: **Formative** during, **summative** after; process, output, outcome and impact evaluation.
blocks.th: RCTs (**Banerjee and Duflo**, Nobel 2019); quasi-experimental designs.
blocks.in: NITI's **DMEO**; outcome budgeting since 2005-06; third-party concurrent evaluation.
blocks.w: Outputs are easy to count; **outcomes are attributable only with design**.

blocks.x: **Formulation** failure (wrong causal theory), **implementation** failure, **compliance** failure, **political** failure.

blocks.in: Demonetisation debated as formulation; open defecation as behaviour and compliance; farm laws as political failure.
blocks.gl: US prohibition as classic formulation failure.
blocks.w: Naming **which failure** is what separates analysis from complaint.

blocks.x: Decisions grounded in data and behavioural insight rather than assertion.
blocks.th: **Thaler and Sunstein**; nudge, **sludge**, boost.
blocks.in: Economic Survey 2018-19's 'Nudge: from BBBP to BADLAV'; 'Give It Up' LPG; default enrolment in APY; Swachh Bharat behaviour campaigns.
blocks.w: Removing **sludge** — friction in accessing entitlements — often beats adding nudges.

blocks.x: In a federal polity many policies can be **designed centrally but only delivered by states**.

blocks.in: GST Council; CSS with 60:40 sharing; Single Nodal Agency; states' complaint that conditionality distorts priorities.
blocks.w: Central design plus state delivery makes **implementation the federal question**.

blocks.x: Systematic examination of procedures to cut steps, time and cost.
blocks.th: Taylor's method applied to the office; O&M divisions.
blocks.in: DARPG's special campaigns clearing crores of files; cutting the levels a file crosses to four.
blocks.w: Process cleaning is a **governance intervention**, not housekeeping.

blocks.x: Superior and subordinate jointly set measurable objectives against which performance is reviewed.
blocks.th: **Peter Drucker**.
blocks.in: **RFD (Results Framework Document)** from 2009-10 with success indicators and weights; outcome budgeting.
blocks.w: MBO fails where objectives are **imposed rather than negotiated**.

blocks.x: Network techniques that map task dependencies and identify the **critical path** that determines project duration.
blocks.th: Operations research.
blocks.in: Metro and highway project scheduling; PM Gati Shakti's layered planning.
blocks.w: Delay on the **critical path** is the only delay that moves the completion date.

blocks.x: Continuous, incremental improvement owned by everyone, with the customer defining quality.
blocks.th: **Deming**, **Juran**; Japanese Kaizen.
blocks.in: Sevottam's service-quality modules; ISO certification of government offices.
blocks.w: TQM in government founders where the **'customer' cannot exit**.

blocks.x: Radical redesign of a process rather than incremental improvement — start from the outcome, not the existing steps.
blocks.th: **Hammer and Champy**.
blocks.in: Faceless assessment in income tax; single-window clearances; DBT replacing a chain of intermediaries.
blocks.w: Digitising a bad process only makes it **fail faster** — redesign first.

blocks.x: **G2C, G2B, G2G, G2E**, maturing through presence → interaction → transaction → transformation.
blocks.th: UN e-government maturity models.
blocks.in: NeGP (2006, 27 mission mode projects) → Digital India (2015) → **DPI**; UMANG, DigiLocker, e-Office, GeM, PFMS, e-Courts; **CSCs** as the assisted layer.
blocks.w: India's distinctive move is **layered public infrastructure**, not monolithic portals.

blocks.x: Real-time measurement changes behaviour by making performance visible and comparable.
blocks.th: Management information systems; competitive federalism.
blocks.in: Aspirational Districts' delta ranking on 49 indicators; NJDG; PRAGATI reviews.
blocks.w: Ranking plus a **named responsible officer** moves outcomes without new money.

blocks.x: Prediction and triage at scale, with accountability that cannot be delegated to a model.
blocks.th: **NITI's Responsible AI** principles; **Puttaswamy** proportionality.
blocks.in: IndiaAI Mission; AI in tax scrutiny selection, crop assessment, grievance routing.
blocks.gl: Dutch childcare benefits scandal, where an algorithm produced mass wrongful accusations.
blocks.w: Insist on a **human in the loop for adverse decisions** and on explainability.

blocks.x: Independent measurement of satisfaction, not agency-reported closure.
blocks.th: Social accountability tools — citizen report cards, community scorecards.
blocks.in: CPGRAMS' **Independent Feedback Unit** calling citizens back; Swachh Survekshan citizen feedback.
blocks.gl: Bangalore citizen report cards (Public Affairs Centre).
blocks.w: An output measure the agency controls **will be gamed**; an independent outcome measure will not.

blocks.x: **Monetary** manages money and credit through the central bank; **fiscal** manages taxation and expenditure through the budget.

blocks.in: MPC with a **4% ±2%** CPI target; Budget's fiscal path; the RBI-government coordination question.
blocks.w: Coordination matters because **fiscal dominance** would defeat inflation targeting.

blocks.w: Where the money goes is where the **policy actually is**.

blocks.th: **Pyhrr** for ZBB; Hoover Commission coined performance budgeting.
blocks.in: ZBB tried from 1987 with little effect; outcome budgeting since 2005-06; Gender Budget Statement since 2005-06.
blocks.w: Each type answers a **different question** — control, management or planning.

blocks.in: Presentation on 1 February; DRSC scrutiny of demands; the **guillotine**; Appropriation Bill (Art. 114); Finance Bill (Art. 117); PFMS in execution; CAG then PAC.
blocks.w: Most demands are voted **under the guillotine, without discussion**.

blocks.x: **Vote on Account, supplementary, additional, excess, exceptional, token grant, vote of credit**.

blocks.in: Excess grants regularised only after PAC scrutiny; a token grant raises a discussion on a new service.
blocks.w: Knowing which instrument fits which situation is a **standing question type**.

blocks.in: Small savings and provident funds sit in the Public Account; charged expenditure is non-votable but discussable.
blocks.w: The three funds encode **three different degrees of legislative control**.

blocks.in: Departmentalisation of accounts (1976) separated audit from accounts; PAC examines CAG reports.
blocks.w: **Propriety audit** — wisdom, faithfulness, economy — is the most contested and most valuable form.

blocks.th: Ambedkar called the CAG the most important officer under the Constitution.
blocks.in: 2G, coal and Ayushman Bharat performance audits.
blocks.gl: NAO reporting to the UK Parliament.
blocks.w: Three limits to name: **PPPs sit awkwardly in jurisdiction, the audit-to-PAC lag blunts consequence, and findings carry no enforcement**.

blocks.th: **Integrated Financial Adviser scheme (1975)** placing the FA under dual control.
blocks.in: The design question: does proximity to the ministry improve advice or capture it?
blocks.w: Dual control is a deliberate trade of **independence for relevance**.

blocks.x: Statutory limits on deficit and debt to bind future governments against short-termism.

blocks.w: India moved from a **deficit anchor to a debt path** — that shift is the current answer.

blocks.x: The **saptanga** seven limbs — swami, amatya, janapada, durga, kosha, danda, mitra — with **yogakshema** as the ruler's purpose.

blocks.in: Cited as India's indigenous administrative theory; anticipates the administrative state.
blocks.gl: Contrasted with Machiavelli, who lacked the welfare premise.
blocks.w: India had a **theory of administration** two millennia before Wilson.

blocks.x: **Mansabdari** with zat and sawar ranks, **jagir** assignments, and the **zabti** revenue system.

blocks.in: The land-revenue apparatus the British inherited and adapted; the district as a revenue unit predates the Collector.
blocks.gl: Ottoman timar system as a parallel.
blocks.w: Continuity of the **revenue foundation** across regimes is the point to make.

blocks.in: The office still fuses revenue, magistracy, elections, disaster and development coordination.
blocks.gl: French prefect as the nearest analogue.
blocks.w: The Collector is a **colonial instrument carrying a democratic mandate**.

blocks.in: The lineage of today's UPSC and the all-India services.
blocks.w: Indianisation was conceded **slowly and under pressure**, never granted.

blocks.th: **Muddiman Committee (1924)**; Motilal Nehru and Jinnah in the minority.
blocks.in: The standing example of a **structurally flawed reform** that no amount of tinkering could save.
blocks.w: Dyarchy failed because it split **responsibility from resources**.

blocks.x: India retained the steel frame and the district system while adding a developmental and welfare mandate.
blocks.th: **Gorwala (1951)** found administration 'not equipped to shoulder the tasks of a welfare state'; **Appleby (1953, 1956)**.

blocks.gl: Post-colonial states that dismantled versus retained colonial services.
blocks.w: India chose **continuity of instrument with change of purpose** — the source of its central tension.

blocks.in: Article 14 non-arbitrariness; DPSPs as directions to the administration; Article 38 and 39 as welfare mandates.
blocks.w: Administrative discretion is exercised **inside a value framework**, not outside it.

blocks.th: **Wheare** — 'quasi-federal'; **Granville Austin** — 'cooperative federalism' and the seamless web.
blocks.in: Strong Centre with residuary powers, Articles 256-257 directions, Article 365 sanction.
blocks.w: India is **federal in form, unitary in spirit** — but increasingly bargained in practice.

blocks.in: Ordinance power (Art. 123), delegated legislation, tribunals — each a functional overlap.
blocks.w: India secures the **purpose** of separation — no concentration — without its form.

blocks.th: **Maneka (1978)**; **Puttaswamy (2017)** and the **proportionality test**.
blocks.in: Preventive detention (*Ameena Begum*, 2023), internet shutdowns (*Anuradha Bhasin*, 2020), surveillance and DPDP exemptions.
blocks.w: Apply the **four-step proportionality test** rather than asserting a balance.

blocks.t: Chief Minister and Council of Ministers

blocks.x: India's federalism is **asymmetric by design**, not by exception.

blocks.in: Fazl Ali Commission (1955) and the SRA 1956; Telangana (2014); J&K Reorganisation (2019); Sixth Schedule councils in the North-East.

blocks.x: Divisions, regional offices and development boards mediate between state and district.

blocks.t: District as the unit of development

blocks.w: India's urbanisation is **under-counted and therefore under-governed**.
